steps.message:
# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the
source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a
defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs
the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed.

Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and
the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero.

The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs:

```bash
bash run_experiment.sh
```

The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8
bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32,
temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU
layout. Do not add format reward or any auxiliary reward, and do not alter
data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader reads only fresh files under
`experiment_logs`: the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric, cross-checked
against verl's own per-step file log and the probe dumps the run writes, with
the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256. Copying or
fabricating metrics scores zero.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-recorded_run}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}

RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug

printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"

cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=4 \
  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
  data.max_response_length=32 \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=2026 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.05 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.fsdp_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode=async \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.35 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=512 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs=16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.temperature=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False \
  reward_model.reward_manager=naive \
  trainer.logger='[console,wandb,file]' \
  trainer.project_name=AutoRLBench-Minimal-RL \
  trainer.experiment_name="${RUN_NAME}" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_epochs=4 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=4 \
  trainer.default_local_dir="${LOG_DIR}/checkpoints-disabled" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations" \
  trainer.log_val_generations=4 \
  +trainer.log_base_model_kl=True \
  +trainer.log_final_policy_health=True \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_DIR}/train.log"

- `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement = 0.10476375009925555` — this is LOW (bad). Only 10% agreement between actor and rollout policies.
- `val-health/base_reference_mae = 0.0` — good (base model reference has zero MAE, meaning reference == base).
- `val-health/base_reference_consistency = 1.0` — good.

So the defect is that the actor (trained LoRA) policy disagrees massively with the rollout (vLLM) policy. This is the classic "vLLM rollout doesn't pick up the LoRA adapter updates" bug.

Note `base_reference_mae = 0.0` and `base_reference_consistency = 1.0` means the reference model matches the base model exactly (it's frozen). But actor_rollout_policy_mae is 2.256 — meaning the actor weights (with the PiSSA LoRA update applied) don't match the vLLM engine's weights.

And `critic/score/mean = 0.0`, rewards all 0.0, advantages all 0.0. `actor/entropy` is ~2.2 (nonzero), and `rollout_corr/kl` is substantial (2.89-3.57), with `rollout_corr/training_ppl` huge (1600-4900). 

Wait, so the key signal: rewards are all 0 (GSM8K accuracy 0.0 across all steps), which is plausible for a 0.5B model on GSM8K with only 16 training samples and 32 token responses — it might genuinely get 0 accuracy. But the health metric `actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256` and `agreement = 0.105` indicates the actor policy and rollout policy are out of sync — the classic bug.

Also `critic/score/mean=0.0` with all-zero rewards means GRPO has zero advantage, so pg_loss=0, grad_norm=0. That's expected when all rewards are identical (all 0), so the actor isn't learning anything. But that's the reward signal being degenerate, which is not necessarily the injected defect — the task says "do not alter data, model, budget or metric logging" and "Do not add format reward." So the reward being 0 might be a genuine property... but wait, the task says the graded metric is "the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric, cross-checked against verl's own per-step file log and the probe dumps."

So the health metric we care about is `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` (and agreement). A healthy experiment should have low MAE (near 0) and high agreement (near 1) between actor and rollout on the final step. Here MAE=2.256 and agreement=0.105 — unhealthy.

The vLLM rollout worker loads the model for generation. The "health" instrumentation computes actor policy vs rollout policy on some probe sequences. The MAE of 2.256 in log-prob space is huge.

In the PiSSA setup, the reference model should be the residual base model, and the "base" is the source Qwen2.5-0.5B. If the base reference MAE is 0, reference == base, i.e., the reference worker is computing log probs with the residual base, and "base" is... hmm.

    def _validate(self):
        data_source_lst = []
        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
        log_final_policy_health = self.config.trainer.get("log_final_policy_health", False) and (
            self.global_steps >= self.total_training_steps
        )
        health_token_count = 0.0
        actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum = 0.0
        base_reference_abs_diff_sum = 0.0

        # Lists to collect samples for the table
        sample_inputs = []
        sample_outputs = []
        sample_gts = []
        sample_scores = []
        sample_turns = []
        sample_uids = []

        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)

            if "uid" not in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(test_batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

            # repeat test batch
            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
            )

            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
                return {}

            # Store original inputs
            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
            sample_uids.extend(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"])

            ground_truths = [
                item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in test_batch
            ]
            sample_gts.extend(ground_truths)

            test_gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(test_batch)
            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {
                "eos_token_id": self.tokenizer.eos_token_id,
                "pad_token_id": self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                "recompute_log_prob": False,
                "do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample,
                "validate": True,
                "global_steps": self.global_steps,
            }
            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")

            # pad to be divisible by dp_size
            size_divisor = (
                self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
                if not self.async_rollout_mode
                else self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
            )
            test_gen_batch_padded, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(test_gen_batch, size_divisor)
            if not self.async_rollout_mode:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)
            else:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)

            # unpad
            test_output_gen_batch = unpad_dataproto(test_output_gen_batch_padded, pad_size=pad_size)

            print("validation generation end")

            # Store generated outputs
            output_ids = test_output_gen_batch.batch["responses"]
            output_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in output_ids]
            sample_outputs.extend(output_texts)

            test_batch = test_batch.union(test_output_gen_batch)
            test_batch.meta_info["validate"] = True

            if log_final_policy_health:
                response_mask = test_batch.batch["response_mask"].float()
                health_token_count += float(response_mask.sum().item())

                actor_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(test_batch)
                if "rollout_log_probs" not in test_batch.batch:
                    raise RuntimeError("final policy-health validation requires rollout_log_probs")
                actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum += float(
                    (
                        (actor_log_prob.batch["old_log_probs"] - test_batch.batch["rollout_log_probs"]).abs()
                        * response_mask
                    )
                    .sum()
                    .item()
                )

                actual_base_ref = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_base_ref_log_prob(test_batch)
                expected_base_ref = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob(test_batch)
                base_reference_abs_diff_sum += float(
                    (
                        (
                            actual_base_ref.batch["base_ref_log_prob"]
                            - expected_base_ref.batch["expected_base_ref_log_prob"]
                        ).abs()
                        * response_mask
                    )
                    .sum()
                    .item()
                )

            # evaluate using reward_function
            if self.val_reward_fn is None:
                raise ValueError("val_reward_fn must be provided for validation.")
            result = self.val_reward_fn(test_batch, return_dict=True)
            reward_tensor = result["reward_tensor"]
            scores = reward_tensor.sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
            sample_scores.extend(scores)

            reward_extra_infos_dict["reward"].extend(scores)
            if "reward_extra_info" in result:
                for key, lst in result["reward_extra_info"].items():
                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key].extend(lst)

            # collect num_turns of each prompt
            if "__num_turns__" in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                sample_turns.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["__num_turns__"])

            data_source_lst.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch.get("data_source", ["unknown"] * reward_tensor.shape[0]))

        self._maybe_log_val_generations(inputs=sample_inputs, outputs=sample_outputs, scores=sample_scores)

        # dump generations
        val_data_dir = self.config.trainer.get("validation_data_dir", None)
        if val_data_dir:
            self._dump_generations(
                inputs=sample_inputs,
                outputs=sample_outputs,
                gts=sample_gts,
                scores=sample_scores,
                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_dict,
                dump_path=val_data_dir,
            )

        for key_info, lst in reward_extra_infos_dict.items():
            assert len(lst) == 0 or len(lst) == len(sample_scores), f"{key_info}: {len(lst)=}, {len(sample_scores)=}"

        data_sources = np.concatenate(data_source_lst, axis=0)

        data_src2var2metric2val = process_validation_metrics(data_sources, sample_uids, reward_extra_infos_dict)
        metric_dict = {}
        for data_source, var2metric2val in data_src2var2metric2val.items():
            core_var = "acc" if "acc" in var2metric2val else "reward"
            for var_name, metric2val in var2metric2val.items():
                n_max = max([int(name.split("@")[-1].split("/")[0]) for name in metric2val.keys()])
                for metric_name, metric_val in metric2val.items():
                    if (
                        (var_name == core_var)
                        and any(metric_name.startswith(pfx) for pfx in ["mean", "maj", "best"])
                        and (f"@{n_max}" in metric_name)
                    ):
                        metric_sec = "val-core"
                    else:
                        metric_sec = "val-aux"
                    pfx = f"{metric_sec}/{data_source}/{var_name}/{metric_name}"
                    metric_dict[pfx] = metric_val

        if len(sample_turns) > 0:
            sample_turns = np.concatenate(sample_turns)
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/min"] = sample_turns.min()
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/max"] = sample_turns.max()
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/mean"] = sample_turns.mean()

        if log_final_policy_health:
            if health_token_count <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError("final policy-health validation observed no response tokens")
            actor_rollout_mae = actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum / health_token_count
            base_reference_mae = base_reference_abs_diff_sum / health_token_count
            metric_dict["val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae"] = actor_rollout_mae
            metric_dict["val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement"] = float(np.exp(-actor_rollout_mae))
            metric_dict["val-health/base_reference_mae"] = base_reference_mae
            metric_dict["val-health/base_reference_consistency"] = float(np.exp(-base_reference_mae))

        return metric_dict

    def init_workers(self):
        """Initialize distributed training workers using Ray backend.

        Creates:
        1. Ray resource pools from configuration
        2. Worker groups for each role (actor, critic, etc.)
        """
        self.resource_pool_manager.create_resource_pool()

        self.resource_pool_to_cls = {pool: {} for pool in self.resource_pool_manager.resource_pool_dict.values()}

        # create actor and rollout
        actor_role = Role.ActorRolloutRef if Role.ActorRolloutRef in self.role_worker_mapping else Role.ActorRollout
        if self.hybrid_engine:
            resource_pool = self.resource_pool_manager.get_resource_pool(actor_role)
            actor_rollout_cls = RayClassWithInitArgs(
                cls=self.role_worker_mapping[actor_role],
                config=self.config.actor_rollout_ref,
                role=str(actor_role),
            )
            self.resource_pool_to_cls[resource_pool][str(actor_role)] = actor_rollout_cls
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError

# TODO(sgm): support FSDP hybrid shard for larger model
        self.device_mesh = create_device_mesh(world_size=world_size, fsdp_size=self.config.actor.fsdp_config.fsdp_size)

        # build device mesh for Ulysses Sequence Parallel
        self.ulysses_device_mesh = None
        self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size = self.config.actor.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1)
        dp = world_size // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
        if self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size > 1:
            self.ulysses_device_mesh = init_device_mesh(
                device_name, mesh_shape=(dp, self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size), mesh_dim_names=["dp", "sp"]
            )

        # create training dispatch
        if self.ulysses_device_mesh is not None:
            is_collect = self.ulysses_device_mesh["sp"].get_local_rank() == 0
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info(
                "actor", dp_rank=self.ulysses_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank(), is_collect=is_collect
            )
        else:
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info("actor", dp_rank=self.rank, is_collect=True)

        self.ulysses_sharding_manager = FSDPUlyssesShardingManager(self.ulysses_device_mesh)
        self._lora_rank = self.config.model.get("lora_rank", 0)
        self._is_lora = self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path") is not None or self._lora_rank > 0
        # True when the base model weights were modified during adapter init (PiSSA/MiLoRA).
        # In that case disable_adapter() returns W_res != W_pretrained, so ref computation
        # must use the saved initial adapter weights instead of disabling the adapter.
        self._is_svd_init = self.config.model.get("lora_residual_base", False)
        self._init_lora_state: dict = {}  # {param_name: CPU tensor} saved before FSDP wrap
        self._svd_ref_adapter_name: str | None = None
        self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged = False

        self.role = role
        assert self.role in ["actor", "rollout", "ref", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]

        self._is_actor = self.role in ["actor", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self._is_rollout = self.role in ["rollout", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self._is_ref = self.role in ["ref", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self.use_orig_params = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("use_orig_params", False)
        if self._is_lora or self.config.model.get("use_dora", False):
            # Keep PEFT trainable params as original tensors so FSDP does not flatten
            # them together with frozen base weights and silently skip updates.
            self.use_orig_params = True

        # TODO(haibin.lin):
        # As of now the type of config is DictConfig, if we assign config.profiler with ProfilerConfig,
        # it will actually convert the ProfilerConfig dataclass back to a DictConfig.
        # We can still use ProfilerConfig for testing purpose (tests/utils/test_nvtx_profile.py)
        # as they provides DictConfig-like interface
        # The benefit of creating the dataclass config is to perform validation during __post_init__
        if self._is_actor:
            omega_profiler_config = config.actor.get("profiler", {})
        elif self._is_rollout:
            # NOTE: In colocation mode, rollout config may not take effect (follow the actor config)
            # This is for extendability in AsyncRL cases
            omega_profiler_config = config.rollout.get("profiler", {})
        elif self._is_ref:
            omega_profiler_config = config.ref.get("profiler", {})
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid role {self.role}, should be one of "
                "['actor', 'rollout', 'ref', 'actor_rollout', 'actor_rollout_ref']"
            )
        # omega_profiler_config is DictConfig
        # profiler_config is a ProfilerConfig dataclass
        profiler_config = omega_conf_to_dataclass(omega_profiler_config, dataclass_type=ProfilerConfig)
        if omega_profiler_config.get("tool", None) in ["npu", "nsys", "torch", "torch_memory"]:
            tool_config = omega_conf_to_dataclass(
                omega_profiler_config.get("tool_config", {}).get(omega_profiler_config.get("tool"))
            )
        else:
            tool_config = None
        DistProfilerExtension.__init__(
            self, DistProfiler(rank=self.rank, config=profiler_config, tool_config=tool_config)
        )

        self._is_offload_param = False
        self._is_offload_optimizer = False
        if self._is_actor:
            self._is_offload_param = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("param_offload", False)
            self._is_offload_optimizer = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("optimizer_offload", False)
        elif self._is_ref:
            # TODO: it seems that manual offload is slowly than FSDP offload
            self._is_offload_param = self.config.ref.fsdp_config.get("param_offload", False)

        # normalize config
        if self._is_actor:
            self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size *= self.config.rollout.n
            self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size //= self.device_mesh.size() // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
            assert self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size > 0, (
                f"ppo_mini_batch_size {self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size} should be larger than 0 after "
                f"normalization"
            )
            # micro bsz
            if self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None:
                self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size //= (
                    self.device_mesh.size() // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
                )
                self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu = self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size

            if enable_gradient_checkpointing:
                actor_module.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})

        if self._is_lora:
            print("Applying LoRA to actor module")
            actor_module.enable_input_require_grads()

            lora_adapter_path = self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path")
            if lora_adapter_path is not None:
                from copy import deepcopy

                from peft import PeftConfig, PeftModel, set_peft_model_state_dict
                from peft.utils.save_and_load import load_peft_weights

                print(f"Loading pre-trained LoRA adapter to {role} from: {lora_adapter_path}")

                # Copy adapter to local if needed
                local_adapter_path = copy_to_local(lora_adapter_path, use_shm=self.config.model.get("use_shm", False))

                adapter_config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(local_adapter_path)
                if self._is_svd_init:
                    # The checkpoint at model.path is already W_res. Re-running
                    # PiSSA/OLoRA initialization here would subtract another SVD
                    # delta before the saved adapter tensors are loaded.
                    adapter_config.init_lora_weights = False

                actor_module = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
                    actor_module,
                    local_adapter_path,
                    is_trainable=True,
                    config=adapter_config,
                    # PiSSA/SVD-init needs real adapter tensors during its
                    # initialization; meta tensors cannot accept the computed
                    # CUDA factors via set_data().
                    low_cpu_mem_usage=not self._is_svd_init,
                )
                peft_config = actor_module.peft_config["default"]
                # Ensure task_type is TaskType enum, not string
                if isinstance(peft_config.task_type, str):
                    peft_config.task_type = TaskType.CAUSAL_LM

                # For SVD-init adapters (PiSSA/MiLoRA) the base layer stores
                # W_res = W_pretrained - delta_init, so disable_adapter() gives
                # the wrong ref. Save the initial adapter and load a frozen copy as
                # a dedicated reference adapter so the correct ref path stays on the
                # standard PEFT forward without FSDP summon_full_params.
                if self._is_svd_init:
                    deferred = 0
                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if "lora_A" not in name and "lora_B" not in name:
                            continue
                        if getattr(param, "is_meta", False):
                            deferred += 1
                            continue
                        self._init_lora_state[name] = param.data.clone().cpu()

                    self._svd_ref_adapter_name = "_base_ref"
                    # Build the frozen copy from an init-disabled config as well;
                    # load_adapter() would read the on-disk PiSSA config and
                    # mutate W_res a second time.
                    ref_config = deepcopy(peft_config)
                    ref_config.inference_mode = True
                    ref_config.init_lora_weights = False
                    actor_module.add_adapter(
                        self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                        ref_config,
                        low_cpu_mem_usage=False,
                    )
                    ref_state = load_peft_weights(local_adapter_path, device="cpu")
                    set_peft_model_state_dict(
                        actor_module,
                        ref_state,
                        adapter_name=self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                    )
                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if f".{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}." in name:
                            param.requires_grad = False

                    if self.rank == 0:
                        if deferred > 0:
                            print(
                                f"[SVD-init ref] Deferred saving {deferred} initial adapter parameters "
                                "until after FSDP materialization."
                            )
                        else:
                            print(
                                f"[SVD-init ref] Saved {len(self._init_lora_state)} "
                                f"initial adapter parameters for correct ref computation."
                            )
                        print(
                            f"[SVD-init ref] Loaded frozen reference adapter '{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}' "
                            "for correct base-model KL computation."
                        )
                disabled_dropout = self._disable_lora_dropout(actor_module)
                if self.rank == 0 and disabled_dropout > 0:
                    print(f"[LoRA] Disabled {disabled_dropout} LoRA dropout modules on loaded adapter")
                self._maybe_freeze_lora_A(actor_module)

            else:
                # Convert config to regular Python types before creating PEFT model
                lora_config = {
                    "task_type": TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
                    "r": self.config.model.lora_rank,
                    "lora_alpha": self.config.model.lora_alpha,
                    "use_dora": self.config.model.use_dora,
                    "target_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.target_modules),
                    "exclude_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.exclude_modules),
                    "bias": "none",
                }
                if self.config.model.get("use_adalora", False):
                    adalora_config = {
                        "task_type": TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
                        "init_r": self.config.model.get("adalora_init_r") or self.config.model.lora_rank,
                        "target_r": self.config.model.get("adalora_target_r") or self.config.model.lora_rank,
                        "lora_alpha": self.config.model.lora_alpha,
                        "target_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.target_modules),
                        "beta1": self.config.model.get("adalora_beta1", 0.85),
                        "beta2": self.config.model.get("adalora_beta2", 0.85),
                        "tinit": self.config.model.get("adalora_tinit", 0),
                        "tfinal": self.config.model.get("adalora_tfinal", 0),
                        "deltaT": self.config.model.get("adalora_delta_t", 1),
                        "total_step": self.config.actor.optim.get("total_training_steps", 0),
                        "orth_reg_weight": self.config.model.get("adalora_orth_reg_weight", 0.5),
                    }
                    actor_module = get_peft_model(actor_module, AdaLoraConfig(**adalora_config))
                    actor_module.to(torch_dtype)
                else:
                    actor_module = get_peft_model(actor_module, LoraConfig(**lora_config))
                disabled_dropout = self._disable_lora_dropout(actor_module)
                if self.rank == 0 and disabled_dropout > 0:
                    print(f"[LoRA] Disabled {disabled_dropout} LoRA dropout modules on actor")
                self._maybe_freeze_lora_A(actor_module)
                init_count = _init_lora_a_params(
                    actor_module,
                    init_method=self.config.model.get("lora_A_init_method", "default"),
                    wavelet=self.config.model.get("lora_A_wavelet", "haar"),
                )
                if self.rank == 0 and init_count > 0:
                    init_desc = f"method={self.config.model.get('lora_A_init_method')}"
                    if self.config.model.get("lora_A_init_method") == "wavelet_orth":
                        init_desc += f" wavelet={self.config.model.get('lora_A_wavelet', 'haar')}"
                    print(f"Applied LoRA-A init {init_desc} to {init_count} actor matrices.")

        self.use_orig_params = fsdp_config.get("use_orig_params", False)
        if self._is_lora or self.config.model.get("use_dora", False) or self.config.model.get("use_adalora", False):
            self.use_orig_params = True
            if self.rank == 0:
                print("[actor model] Enabling use_orig_params=True for LoRA/DoRA/AdaLoRA under FSDP.")
        if self.config.actor.get("freeze_vision_tower", False):
            vision_tower = get_vl_model_vision_tower(actor_module)
            if vision_tower is not None:
                vision_tower.requires_grad_(False)
                self.use_orig_params = True
                if self.rank == 0:
                    print("[actor model] Vision tower is set to not trainable.")
            else:
                if self.rank == 0:
                    print("[actor model] No vision tower found.")

657

659	                    # Build the frozen copy from an init-disabled config as well;

662	                    ref_config = deepcopy(peft_config)

665	                    actor_module.add_adapter(

The `base_reference_mae = 0.0` means base reference is healthy. But actor_rollout_policy_mae is 2.256, which is large — agreement only 10%.

In verl, when using LoRA, the LoRA weights need to be synced to the vLLM rollout worker. If sync fails, the rollout policy keeps using stale/initial weights while the actor is being trained, causing big MAE.

Actually the issue may be that vLLM sync of lora_delta adds B@A to the base model weights, but the base model in vLLM was loaded as W_res (residual base), not W_pretrained. Let me investigate.

Actually, wait. Let me re-read. The debug `rollout_sync_initial` shows `rollout_sync_mode: svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` and `rollout_model_path: residual_base`. Then during the update sync (`rollout_sync_latest`), it uses `lora_delta` mode: it computes the LoRA delta (B@A - presumably) and uploads to vLLM, which applies it to W_pretrained base that was loaded during initial sync.         # used for LoRA
        self.base_sync_done: bool = "dummy" not in self.config.rollout.load_format
        self.layered_summon = self.config.rollout.get("layered_summon", False)

        # 5. switch to trainer mode
        # NOTE: It's critical that hybrid engine in trainer mode initially to load checkpoint.
        # For sync mode, we directly switch to trainer mode here.
        # For async mode, we can't call run_until_complete here, so we will switch to trainer mode in AgentLoopManager.
        if rollout_config.mode == "sync" and self._is_actor:
            loop = get_event_loop()
            loop.run_until_complete(self.trainer_mode())

    async def rollout_mode(self):
        """Context switch hybridengine to rollout mode."""
        aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)

        peft_config = None
        rollout_sync_mode = "full_weights"
        peft_model = getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        if hasattr(peft_model, "peft_config"):  # LoRA / DoRA
            peft_config = peft_model.peft_config.get("default", None)
            if self._is_svd_init and not self.base_sync_done:
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout first sync for SVD-init adapters uses the original pretrained base model "
                    "instead of merged residual weights so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path."
                )
                params = self._collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params(peft_config)
                # SVD-init variants (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA residual-base bundles) still run vLLM
                # with LoRA wrappers enabled, so pretrained full weights must target base_layer.*
                # keys just like the normal first-sync LoRA path.
                params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights"
            elif getattr(peft_config, "use_dora", False) or str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "")).endswith(
                "ADALORA"
            ):
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout sync uses merged full weights for DoRA/AdaLoRA because "
                    "vLLM adapter loading is unsupported or unsafe for this PEFT type."
                )
                params = collect_merged_peft_params(module=self.actor_module_fsdp)
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "merged_full_weights"
            else:
                params = collect_lora_params(
                    module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                    layered_summon=self.config.rollout.get("layered_summon", False),
                    base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done,
                )
                rollout_sync_mode = "lora_delta" if self.base_sync_done else "initial_base_plus_lora_named_weights"
                if not self.base_sync_done:
                    params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
        else:
            params = self.actor_module_fsdp.state_dict()

        if self.rank == 0:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                sync_stage = "rollout_sync_initial" if not self.base_sync_done else "rollout_sync_latest"
                debug_path = _write_rollout_policy_debug(
                    sync_stage,
                    {
                        "experiment_name": str(getattr(self, "experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                        "rank": int(self.rank),
                        "base_sync_done_before": bool(self.base_sync_done),
                        "is_svd_init": bool(self._is_svd_init),
                        "is_lora": bool(self._is_lora),
                        "rollout_sync_mode": rollout_sync_mode,
                        "rollout_model_path": str(self.config.model.path),
                        "rollout_has_peft_config": peft_config is not None,
                        "peft_type": str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "none")) if peft_config is not None else "none",
                        "active_adapter": (
                            peft_model.active_adapters[0] if getattr(peft_model, "active_adapters", None) else None
                        ),
                        "lora_adapter_path": str(self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path", "")),
                    },
                )
                print(f"[DEBUG rollout policy] wrote {debug_path}")

        params = convert_weight_keys(
            params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        )

        # Special handling for LoRA with sleep_level=2:
        # When sleep_level=2, base model weights are destroyed during each sleep cycle.
        # separately collect and update LoRA weights and base model weights through their respective interfaces.
        # Here: params contains LoRA weights, base_model_params contains base model weights.
        if peft_config is not None and getattr(self.rollout, "sleep_level", None) == 2:
            base_model_params = collect_lora_params(
                module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                layered_summon=self.layered_summon,
                base_sync_done=False,
            )
            base_model_params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in base_model_params.items()}
            base_model_params = convert_weight_keys(
                base_model_params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
            )

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)

        set_expandable_segments(False)

        if peft_config is not None and self.base_sync_done:
            per_tensor_param = params.items() if isinstance(params, dict) else params  # Fixed: handle dict case
        else:
            device = get_device_id()  # used when fsdp2 set cpu_offload_policy
            per_tensor_param = (
                (name, param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor() if isinstance(param, DTensor) else param)
                for name, param in params.items()
            )

        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            await self.rollout.resume(tags=["weights"])
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After resume weights", logger=logger)

        if peft_config is not None and getattr(self.rollout, "sleep_level", None) == 2:
            per_tensor_base_params = (
                (name, param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor() if isinstance(param, DTensor) else param)
                for name, param in base_model_params.items()
            )
            await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_base_params, base_sync_done=False)
            del base_model_params, per_tensor_base_params

        await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After update_weights", logger=logger)
        del params, per_tensor_param
        aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)
        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            await self.rollout.resume(tags=["kv_cache"])
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After resume kv_cache", logger=logger)

        self.base_sync_done = True
        # important: need to manually set the random states of each tp to be identical.
        self.torch_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        get_torch_device().set_rng_state(self.gen_random_states)

    async def trainer_mode(self):
        """Context switch hybridengine to trainer mode."""
        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            log_gpu_memory_usage("Before rollout offload", logger=logger)
            await self.rollout.release()

async def resume(self, tags: list[str]):
        """Resume rollout weights or kv cache in GPU memory.

        Args:
            tags: weights or kv_cache.
        """
        if self.config.free_cache_engine:
            self.inference_engine.wake_up(tags=tags)

    async def release(self):
        """Release weights and kv cache in GPU memory."""
        if self.config.free_cache_engine:
            self.inference_engine.sleep(level=self.sleep_level)

    async def update_weights(self, weights: Generator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor], None, None], **kwargs):
        """Update the weights of the rollout model.

        Args:
            weights: A generator that yields the name of the weight tensor and the tensor itself.
        """
        peft_config, base_sync_done = kwargs.get("peft_config", None), kwargs.get("base_sync_done", False)
        if peft_config and base_sync_done:
            # In async mode, make sure the old lora is removed before adding the new one
            self.inference_engine.worker.remove_lora(VLLM_LORA_INT_ID)
            lora_tensors = dict(weights)
            lora_request = TensorLoRARequest(
                lora_name=VLLM_LORA_NAME,
                lora_int_id=VLLM_LORA_INT_ID,
                lora_path=VLLM_LORA_PATH,
                peft_config=asdict(peft_config),
                lora_tensors=lora_tensors,
            )
            self.inference_engine.worker.add_lora(lora_request)
            logger.info(f"vLLM load weights, loaded_params: {len(lora_tensors)}")
        else:
            from verl.utils.vllm.patch import patch_vllm_moe_model_weight_loader, patch_vllm_qwen2_packed_weight_loader

            model_runner = self.inference_engine.worker.model_runner
            model = model_runner.model
            patch_vllm_moe_model_weight_loader(model)
            patch_vllm_qwen2_packed_weight_loader()

            # Add the FP8 related logic here as sharding manager has been deprecated.
            # Check if FP8 quantization is enabled and apply appropriate weight loading
            if is_fp8_model(model_runner.vllm_config):
                logger.info(f"FP8 model detected (async): {model_runner.vllm_config.quant_config}")
                # Convert bf16 weights to fp8 format before loading
                loaded_params = load_quanted_weights(weights, model_runner)
                logger.info(f"FP8 weights loaded (async), loaded_params: {len(loaded_params)}")
            else:
                logger.info("Loading standard weights (non-FP8, async)")
                model.load_weights(weights)

    def generate_sequences(self, prompts: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        """Batch generate sequences in sync mode."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    # ==================== server mode public methods ====================

    def get_zeromq_address(self):
        return self.address

In the observed run, `base_reference_mae = 0.0` (consistency = 1.0) — so the two "base reference" paths agree. But the `actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256` (agreement = 0.105), meaning the actor's current policy differs from the rollout policy by a large amount.

The whole point of GRPO with a hybrid engine is: after each update step, the actor weights are synced to the vLLM rollout via `rollout_mode()`. So the rollout policy and the actor policy should be exactly equal. The health metric cross-checks that this synchronization stayed intact.    The user asked to review a staged experiment for health, inspect source/launch script/metrics/rollouts/debug evidence, find defects, repair them in `/workspace`, and write `/workspace/report.md` describing root cause, changed files, and expected metric effect. The experiment uses Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8 LoRA, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32, temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU layout. Do NOT add format/auxiliary rewards, do NOT alter data/model/budget/metric logging, do NOT launch training.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)**: Advantage estimator = GRPO, uses relative advantage within rollout groups
   - **PiSSA (Principal Singular values and Singular vectors Adaptation)**: SVD-initialized LoRA where base = W_res = W_pretrained - delta_init
   - **verl framework**: Ray-based distributed RL training with FSDP actors, vLLM rollout, hybrid engine
   - **Health instrumentation**: `log_final_policy_health` computes MAE between actor log probs and rollout log probs, plus base reference vs expected SVD ref
   - **Rollout sync modes**: `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` (initial), `lora_delta` (subsequent)
   - **Naive reward manager**: Uses default GSM8K reward function for answer extraction and scoring

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`/workspace/run_experiment.sh`** — Launch script with all experiment hyperparameters. Key settings: PiSSA bundle path, target_modules=all-linear, n=4, temperature=0.8, kl_coef=0.05, 4 steps, reward_manager=naive, log_final_policy_health=True, log_base_model_kl=True
   
   - **`/workspace/observed_run/metrics/all_steps.jsonl`** — Critical metrics file showing the defect:
     - ALL 5 steps (0-4): `critic/score/mean: 0.0`, `critic/rewards/mean: 0.0`, `critic/advantages/mean: 0.0`
     - ALL steps: `reward_components/acc_mean: 0.0`, `actor/pg_loss: 0.0`, `actor/grad_norm: 0.0`

     - ALL val: `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1: 0.0`
   
   - **`/workspace/verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`** (lines 550-735) — `_validate()` method with health instrumentation. Computes actor_rollout_mae, base_reference_mae at final step via `compute_base_ref_log_prob` and `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob`

   - **`/workspace/verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py`** — Actor worker with comprehensive PiSSA/SVD-init handling:
     - Lines 362-367: `_is_lora`, `_is_svd_init` flags
     - Lines 600-698: LoRA adapter loading with SVD-init support, frozen reference adapter creation (`_base_ref`)
     - Lines 974-1103: `rollout_mode()` — syncs weights to vLLM, first sync uses `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights`, later uses `lora_delta`
     - Lines 1413-1464: `compute_log_prob()` — handles `is_lora` flag
     - Lines 1518-1545: `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` — context manager to switch to frozen initial adapter
     - Lines 1547-1579: `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor()` — base model log prob computation
     - Lines 1612-1637: `compute_base_ref_log_prob()` and `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob()`

   - **`/workspace/verl/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_rollout.py`** (lines 234-271) — `update_weights()` handles peft_config with base_sync_done flag

   - **`/workspace/verl/verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py`** (lines 611-668) — `collect_lora_params()`, `collect_merged_peft_params()`, `replace_lora_wrapper()`

   - **`/workspace/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8/pissa_adapter/adapter_config.json`** — Adapter targets only `["v_proj", "q_proj"]`, `init_lora_weights: "pissa_niter_2"`, rank 8

   - **`/workspace/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8/bundle_manifest.json`** — Bundle metadata confirming PiSSA setup

   - **Debug probes** (9 files in `observed_run/debug/`):

Every rollout gets reward=0, yielding zero advantages → zero policy gradient loss → zero gradient norm → zero KL loss → model weights never change. The model is stuck at its initial state with zero GSM8K accuracy.

steps.reasoning_content:
The rollout outputs are garbage — the model is producing gibberish. But the validation generation outputs are clean `#### <integer>` format. Interesting. The rollout outputs are pure garbage (Chinese characters, random symbols), while validation outputs look like proper attempts `#### 100`, `#### 20`, etc.

Wait — this is a KEY observation. The rollout outputs during training are complete garbage, but the validation outputs are clean. Why would that be?

The difference: 
- Rollouts use temperature 0.8 (in run_experiment.sh), response length 32
- Validation uses greedy decoding (temperature 0 presumably / do_sample=False)

Actually wait, but garbage like `选项和复数...` and repeated `）` is much worse than typical temperature 0.8 sampling would produce from even a 0.5B model. This looks like the model is producing garbage because... the weights are corrupted or the wrong weights are loaded during rollout.

Actually, let me look more carefully. The debug probes confirmed: `base_sync_done=false, peft_type="none", mode="svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights"` for initial rollout sync. That means on the initial sync, the FULL PRETRAINED weights are loaded into vLLM — NOT the PiSSA-initialized LoRA. So the base model (Qwen2.5-0.5B pretrained) is generating — and a raw pretrained 0.5B without any instruction tuning would produce garbage, especially in these weird "return only ####" instructions.

But also: the PiSSA initialization is SVD-based, meaning the base = W_res = W_pretrained - delta_init. If delta_init is small, base is close to pretrained. So the base model is just a raw pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B, which outputs gibberish.

The validation generations `#### 100`, `#### 20` etc. look surprisingly clean though. There `#### 100` is actually correct format but wrong answer. Hmm, `#### 100` for "Royce takes 40 minutes more than double Rob..." gt=280. `#### 20` for son age gt=25. These are coherent but wrong answers.

Wait, why would validation give coherent outputs while rollout gives garbage? Let me check the validation config — validation likely uses do_sample=False (greedy). But greedy of a raw pretrained model would also be somewhat coherent-ish but the rollout at temp 0.8 gives garbage.

Actually the key question I need to answer is the root cause of "zero rewards". The observed metric is `critic/rewards/mean: 0.0` — every rollout scored 0. Since score=0 for everything, advantage=0, no learning.

But actually, the model outputs being garbage means the reward IS legitimately 0 (all answers wrong). But wait — is "all answers wrong" the real issue, or is there a bug?

Let me reconsider. The critical signal from the summary: 
- `val-health/base_reference_mae: 0.0` and `base_reference_consistency: 1.0` — this means the base reference weight (the frozen SVD residual) exactly matches the expected SVD ref. This is GOOD — PiSSA init is correct.
- `actor_rollout_policy_mae: 2.256` — actor vs rollout policy differ by 2.256. This means the actor (which has the LoRA delta applied) differs from the rollout model. But the rollout model never got updated (no weight delta) — wait, but if there's no weight delta, why would actor and rollout differ?

Actually `actor_rollout_policy_mae` compares log probs of the actor (training model with PiSSA LoRA) vs the rollout model (vLLM). If the rollout uses `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` (full pretrained, NO LoRA), and the actor uses the PiSSA-structured base+LoRA, then:

- actor log prob = P_pissa(W_base + LoRA_delta) where W_base = W_pretrained - delta_init and LoRA starts at delta_init → network = W_pretrained (at init)
- rollout = P(W_pretrained)

At init these should be IDENTICAL mathematically (PiSSA init means base+adapter = original pretrained). So mae should be ~0 if both are equivalent.

But `actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256` with agreement 0.105. That's a significant discrepancy. And `base_reference_mae = 0.0` (perfect match between base ref and expected SVD ref).

Hmm wait — but is the actor's log prob being computed correctly in the rollout's mode? Let me think about what "actor_rollout_policy_mae" actually measures. It's MAE between actor log probs (from compute_log_prob on the ACTOR side, with the LoRA) and rollout log probs (from generate_sequences' log_probs).

Let me reconsider what the actual defect is. The user's framing: "review for health, inspect source/launch script/metrics/rollouts/debug evidence, find defects, repair them". There's a staged defect planted in this experiment. I need to find it.

Key observations so far:
1. All rewards = 0 → all advantages = 0 → pg_loss = 0 → no learning.
2. Rollout outputs are GARBAGE (Chinese characters, random repeated parens) — not just "wrong answers".
3. Validation outputs are coherent but wrong (`#### 100`, `#### 20`).

The garbage rollout outputs are the smoking gun. Why does the rollout produce garbage while validation produces coherent text?

The difference between rollout and validation:
- Rollout: temperature 0.8, do_sample=True, response_length=32
- Validation: probably greedy (do_sample=False)

But more importantly — the initial rollout sync mode is `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights`. This loads the FULL pretrained weights into vLLM. Then subsequent syncs use `lora_delta`. 

Wait, but there's a critical subtlety with PiSSA: At init, the actor's trainable LoRA is initialized to the SVD delta (delta_init), and the base is W_pretrained - delta_init. So actor network = base + adapter = (W - delta_init) + delta_init = W (pretrained). Good.

For the ROLLOUT (vLLM) on first sync: `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` = load full pretrained = W. Same as actor. Good, consistent.

But then the rollout generates garbage. If the actor ALSO generates garbage (same weights), it should be consistent. But validation generated coherent text. Unless validation uses a DIFFERENT model than rollout?

Actually wait. Let me reconsider. The key question: is the model correctly loaded? The garbage output strongly suggests the rollout weights are corrupted/wrongly loaded, OR the tokenizer is mismatched.

Actually! Look at the garbage more carefully: `选项和复数，对于类，那样是，外 出` — Chinese characters. Qwen2.5 is trained on lots of Chinese, so a raw pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B asked in English to do arithmetic might produce Chinese gibberish. This is actually PLAUSIBLE for a raw pretrained 0.5B model. Qwen2.5-0.5B is a base model (not instruct), so it doesn't follow instructions well and its completions are often incoherent.

The validation outputs being coherent `#### 100` is a bit surprising then. Unless... the validation is also garbage but this particular sample happened to be coherent? Let me check all validation outputs.

Actually, let me step back. The REAL question for the report is: what's the DEFECT planted in the experiment? The user said "find defects, repair them". There's a specific bug to find.

Given the constraint "Do NOT alter data/model/budget/metric logging", the defect is likely in the reward function or the rollout setup or the PiSSA handling.

Let me look at the reward function. The summary says reward_manager=naive uses default GSM8K reward. The GSM8K reward extracts the answer via regex. If the model outputs garbage (no `####` match), the reward returns 0. That's correct behavior given garbage outputs.

But the deeper issue: WHY does the model output garbage? Is it expected (raw pretrained 0.5B can't do GSM8K) or is it a defect?

Let me check the validation outputs more, and the reward function code, and the train.log for errors. Also let me check the GSM8K data — the "gts" values (4, 40, 10000, 840) — these look correct for the problems. OK.

Actually, I realize I should focus. Let me look at:
1. The reward function (gsm8k.py) 
2. All validation generations
3. train.log for errors/warnings
4. The debug probes content (already summarized but let me re-verify key facts)

Let me also reconsider the base_reference_mae=0.0 result. That says the base reference (frozen adapter) exactly matches expected SVD ref. Good.

But `actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256`. This is a big mismatch. If actor and rollout are supposed to represent the same policy, why the mismatch? 

Possibility: The rollout's log probs are computed with a DIFFERENT model than the actor. Specifically, the actor computes log_prob with the PiSSA LoRA applied (base + adapter → at init = W_pretrained). The rollout, on first sync, gets `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` = W_pretrained. These should match at init.

Unless: The actor's `compute_log_prob` uses the base+LoRA but the rollout's log_probs come from the generation which used a DIFFERENT base. Hmm.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether the actor is even correctly initialized. The health check `actor_rollout_policy_mae` compares:
1. Actor-side log probs of the rollout's sampled tokens: computed via `compute_log_prob` on the ACTOR model.
2. Rollout-side log probs: the log probs returned by vLLM during generation.

If these match, mae=0. mae=2.256 means they differ substantially.

Hmm, but actually the metric in the summary said `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement: 0.105`. Agreement = fraction of tokens where actor and rollout agree on argmax. 0.105 is essentially random. This suggests the actor and rollout are genuinely DIFFERENT models.

Given `base_reference_mae=0.0` (base ref correct), the frozen base is fine. But the ACTIVE actor (base+LoRA) vs rollout differ.

Wait — could the bug be that the ACTOR's LoRA is initialized to ZERO instead of the SVD delta? If the actor LoRA were zero-initialized, then:
- actor = W_base + 0 = W_pretrained - delta_init (WRONG! missing the SVD delta)
- But base_reference = frozen adapter = delta_init. And expected_svd_base_ref = W but residual... 

Hmm, let me look at the debug probes for actual log prob values. The summary said:
- `actor_update.rank0.json`: diff_mean=0.0, base_ref_mean=-5.34, rollout_vs_current_diff_abs_mean=0.0

Let me actually read the debug probes now.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-recorded_run}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}

RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug

printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"

cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=4 \
  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
  data.max_response_length=32 \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=2026 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \

from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any

import torch

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
from verl.workers.reward_manager import register
from verl.workers.reward_manager.abstract import AbstractRewardManager


@register("naive")
class NaiveRewardManager(AbstractRewardManager):
    """The reward manager."""

    def __init__(self, tokenizer, num_examine, compute_score=None, reward_fn_key="data_source") -> None:
        """
        Initialize the NaiveRewardManager instance.

        Args:
            tokenizer: The tokenizer used to decode token IDs into text.
            num_examine: The number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console for debugging purpose.
            compute_score: A function to compute the reward score. If None, `default_compute_score` will be used.
            reward_fn_key: The key used to access the data source in the non-tensor batch data. Defaults to
                "data_source".
        """
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer  # Store the tokenizer for decoding token IDs
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
        self.reward_fn_key = reward_fn_key  # Store the key for accessing the data source

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor | dict[str, Any]:
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        if "rm_scores" in data.batch.keys():
            if return_dict:
                reward_extra_keys = data.meta_info.get("reward_extra_keys", [])
                reward_extra_info = {key: data.non_tensor_batch[key] for key in reward_extra_keys}
                return {"reward_tensor": data.batch["rm_scores"], "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info}
            else:
                return data.batch["rm_scores"]

        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
        reward_extra_info = defaultdict(list)

        already_print_data_sources = {}

        for i in range(len(data)):
            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem

            prompt_ids = data_item.batch["prompts"]

            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]

            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][:prompt_length].sum()
            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]

            response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][prompt_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)

            ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]
            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch[self.reward_fn_key]
            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("extra_info", {})
            num_turns = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("__num_turns__", None)
            rollout_reward_scores = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_scores", {})
            extra_info["num_turns"] = num_turns
            extra_info["rollout_reward_scores"] = rollout_reward_scores

            score = self.compute_score(
                data_source=data_source,
                solution_str=response_str,
                ground_truth=ground_truth,
                extra_info=extra_info,
            )

            if isinstance(score, dict):
                reward = score["score"]
                # Store the information including original reward
                for key, value in score.items():
                    reward_extra_info[key].append(value)
            else:
                reward = score

            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = reward

            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0

            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
                print("[prompt]", prompt_str)
                print("[response]", response_str)
                print("[ground_truth]", ground_truth)
                if isinstance(score, dict):
                    for key, value in score.items():
                        print(f"[{key}]", value)
                else:
                    print("[score]", score)

        if return_dict:
            return {
                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
                "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info,
            }
        else:
            return reward_tensor

17	_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300
18	
19	
20	def extract_solution(solution_str, method="strict"):
21	    assert method in ["strict", "flexible"]
22	
23	    # Optimization: Regular expression matching on very long strings can be slow.
24	    # For math problems, the final answer is usually at the end.
25	    # We only match on the last 300 characters, which is a safe approximation for 300 tokens.
26	    if len(solution_str) > _SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:
27	        solution_str = solution_str[-_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:]
28	
29	    if method == "strict":
30	        # this also tests the formatting of the model
31	        solutions = re.findall("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
32	        if len(solutions) == 0:
33	            final_answer = None
34	        else:
35	            # take the last solution
36	            final_answer = solutions[-1].replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
37	    elif method == "flexible":
38	        answer = re.findall("(\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
39	        final_answer = None
40	        if len(answer) == 0:
41	            # no reward is there is no answer
42	            pass
43	        else:
44	            invalid_str = ["", "."]
45	            # find the last number that is not '.'
46	            for final_answer in reversed(answer):
47	                if final_answer not in invalid_str:
48	                    break
49	    return final_answer
50	
51	
52	def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
53	    """The scoring function for GSM8k.
54	
55	    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
56	    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.
57	
58	    Args:
59	        solution_str: the solution text
60	        ground_truth: the ground truth
61	        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
62	        format_score: the score for the format
63	        score: the score for the correct answer
64	    """
65	    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
66	    if answer is None:
67	        return 0
68	    else:
69	        if answer == ground_truth:
70	            return score
71	        else:
72	            return format_score

import re

_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300


def extract_solution(solution_str, method="strict"):
    assert method in ["strict", "flexible"]

    # Optimization: Regular expression matching on very long strings can be slow.
    # For math problems, the final answer is usually at the end.
    # We only match on the last 300 characters, which is a safe approximation for 300 tokens.
    if len(solution_str) > _SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:
        solution_str = solution_str[-_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:]

    if method == "strict":
        # this also tests the formatting of the model
        solutions = re.findall("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        if len(solutions) == 0:
            final_answer = None
        else:
            # take the last solution
            final_answer = solutions[-1].replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    elif method == "flexible":
        answer = re.findall("(\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        final_answer = None
        if len(answer) == 0:
            # no reward is there is no answer
            pass
        else:
            invalid_str = ["", "."]
            # find the last number that is not '.'
            for final_answer in reversed(answer):
                if final_answer not in invalid_str:
                    break
    return final_answer


def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
    """The scoring function for GSM8k.

    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.

    Args:
        solution_str: the solution text
        ground_truth: the ground truth
        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
        format_score: the score for the format
        score: the score for the correct answer
    """
    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
    if answer is None:
        return 0
    else:
        if answer == ground_truth:
            return score
        else:
            return format_score

    @DistProfiler.annotate(color="blue", role="actor_compute_log_prob")
    def compute_log_prob(self, data: DataProto):
        # when is_lora is True, we use the actor without lora applied to calculate the log_prob
        # which is mostly used for ref log_prob calculation
        assert self._is_actor
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)

        # Support all hardwares
        from contextlib import nullcontext

        is_lora = data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", False)
        adapter_ctx = self.actor.actor_module.disable_adapter() if is_lora else nullcontext()
        peft_model = getattr(self.actor, "actor_module", None)
        if self.rank == 0:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                debug_path = _write_rollout_policy_debug(
                    "actor_compute_log_prob",
                    {
                        "experiment_name": str(getattr(self, "experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                        "rank": int(self.rank),
                        **_actor_adapter_state_payload(peft_model, {"is_lora_flag": bool(is_lora)}),
                    },
                )
                print(f"[DEBUG actor compute_log_prob policy] wrote {debug_path}")
        # we should always recompute old_log_probs when it is HybridEngine
        data.meta_info["micro_batch_size"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
        data.meta_info["max_token_len"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu
        data.meta_info["use_dynamic_bsz"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz
        data.meta_info["temperature"] = self.config.rollout.temperature
        # perform recompute log_prob
        with self.ulysses_sharding_manager:
            with adapter_ctx:
                output, entropys = self.actor.compute_log_prob(data=data, calculate_entropy=True)
            output = DataProto.from_dict(
                tensors={"old_log_probs": output, "entropys": entropys},
                meta_info={"temperature": self.config.rollout.temperature},
            )

        output = output.to("cpu")

        # https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/fsdp.html#fsdp-notes

        if self.world_size > 1 and fsdp_version(self.actor.actor_module) == 1:

            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor model during compute_log_prob", logger=logger)

        return output
